correctness.rationale: The radical-square-zero multiplication yields an exact independent linear equation on each arrow. A sum of \(t\) commutators gives a vertex coloring by \(2t\) field coordinates; nonzero target coefficients require proper colors, and proper colors make the corresponding arrow equations surjective. This proves necessity/sufficiency, minimum length and maximum width, and the weighted fiber formula by multiplying \(q^{2t}\) or \(q^{2t-1}\) local solution counts. Loops and parallel arrows, characteristic two, and the empty sum are explicitly resolved. The saved verify.py is an independent finite cross-check, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The theorem completely identifies minimum additive commutator length for every element of the commutator subspace in arbitrary finite radical-square-zero quiver algebras, with an exact all-target fiber count and sharp chromatic threshold. It proves unbounded length over each fixed finite field, the explicit 15-dimensional binary boundary, and an orientation-independent weighted graph partition function. These are structurally motivated general invariants rather than a small or arbitrary computation.
